summary: Backend-only regression + RBAC + per-rider plan snapshot verification. 45/45 tests in test_iter51_plan_snapshot_and_rbac.py PASS. Verified: (1) GET /api/plan for demo rider returns valid couch-to-road structure (title, workouts, goals, weekly_load, phases); (2) rider snapshot isolation — mutating db.plans template title in Mongo does NOT change the rider's /api/plan payload (rider stays pinned to their training_plans snapshot with 'definition' + 'snapshot_at'); (3) POST /api/rider/plan {reset_progress:true} re-snapshots from the CURRENT template AND resets plan_state.current_week to 1; (4) idempotency — lazy snapshot creation on first GET, and repeated GETs do NOT reshift snapshot title or snapshot_at; (5) all four plans (couch-to-road, ride-stronger, ride-beyond, build-and-climb) assign and serve GET /api/plan without 500s; (6) Admin RBAC — all 7 /api/plans/* mutations return 401 anonymous / 403 rider, and all 6 /api/admin/* routes return 401 anonymous / 403 rider. Demo state restored: template title 'From Couch to Road', snapshot title 'From Couch to Road', plan_state.current_week=1.

minor.issue: Router-wide dependency `Depends(auth.require_admin)` gates the ENTIRE plans_admin router (server.py:4277), so READ routes are also admin-only: anon=401, rider=403. The review-request contract says only WRITE routes (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) should be admin-gated. Not currently used by the rider frontend (which lists plans via /api/rider/plan), but this contradicts the stated intent and will break any client that expected public plan reads. Consider moving `Depends(require_admin)` onto individual write routes or `dependencies=` overrides on the read routes.

That legacy suite hits /api/plans, /api/plans/{id}, PATCH /weeks/1/days/1, POST /adapt anonymously (no Bearer token). Under the new admin gating every one of those requests now returns 401/403 instead of 200. Not fixed by this iteration (out of scope: fix-vs-report), but the suite is now permanently red until either (a) it authenticates as an admin, or (b) reads are un-gated per the contract.

action_items: Decide whether /api/plans/* READS (GET list, GET by id) should be admin-only. If NO (per stated contract), move `Depends(auth.require_admin)` from the router-level include (server.py:4277) onto each mutation route in plans_admin.py, or apply it via `dependencies=` per-route. If YES, update /app/backend/tests/test_plans_admin_fork.py to authenticate as admin so that legacy suite doesn't stay red.
Consider adding a lightweight assertion at snapshot time that `snapshot_at` never regresses on idempotent GET /api/plan (already verified in iter51 tests, but worth pinning as an invariant).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1980-1989 — snapshot rebuild uses `req.reset_progress or not (existing and existing.get('definition'))`; this is correct AND matches the /api/plan lazy-snapshot in _rider_plan_def (server.py:2989-3006). Confirmed both paths write `id`, `definition`, `snapshot_at` under the scoped user_id.
server.py:3020-3025 — _struct_ctx_for_rider correctly falls back to global _struct_ctx when the snapshot has no weeks, so an empty/malformed snapshot won't 500 the rider.

plans_admin.py:127-244 — writes always call `_persist` which fires `_notify(plan_id)` → `_on_plan_change` (server.py:3028-3035), which reloads the in-memory CTR/RS/RB constants. That means changes to the shared template still affect NEW riders and STATE lookups keyed off in-memory constants; the snapshot only protects rider-facing plan definition reads, which is the desired scope.
seed_data_creation: No new seed data. Test mutations are made directly in Mongo (couch-to-road template title, plan_state.current_week) and restored inside each test's finally block. Rider snapshot was re-snapshotted back to 'From Couch to Road' and plan_state.current_week set to 1 at teardown — verified post-run against db.plans, db.training_plans, db.plan_state.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The plans_admin router at /api/plans is CURRENTLY admin-only for reads too (401 anon, 403 rider). If that changes, /app/backend/tests/test_iter51_plan_snapshot_and_rbac.py::TestAdminRBAC::test_plans_get_gating_documented will start printing different codes — it does not assert them so it will still pass; only the RBAC parametrized mutation tests would need to be revisited if the gating model changes. Snapshot semantics: rider snapshot at db.training_plans (scoped by user_id) has fields {id, definition, snapshot_at}. To assert snapshot isolation without hitting write endpoints, mutate db.plans.{id}.title directly in Mongo and re-GET /api/plan.
rca_of_issue: Not applicable — no bugs found in the tested scope. The two minor items above are contract mismatches (read-route gating) and cascading test failure in a pre-existing suite, not application bugs.
